root_cause.text: In `arch/arm64/kernel/ptrace.c`’s `sve_set_common()`, a prior refactor gated the `TIF_SVE` update behind `system_supports_sme()`, so on systems with SVE but no SME a ptrace write to `NT_ARM_SVE` could save SVE state in `FP_STATE_SVE` format without setting `TIF_SVE`, leaving the task in an inconsistent state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (system_supports_sme())` wrapper around the `switch (type)` that does `target->thread.svcr &= ~SVCR_SM_MASK; set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`, and the CVE text says this bug was introduced when “the setting of TIF_SVE was moved into a block which is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true,” causing “SVE register data [to be] stored in FP_STATE_SVE format but TIF_SVE is clear.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Always apply SVE/SME task mode state updates regardless of system SME support.
intent_record.what: The code removed the outer `if (system_supports_sme())` wrapper around the `switch (type)` block in `sve_set_common()`, so the `switch` on `ARM64_VEC_SVE`/`ARM64_VEC_SME` now executes unconditionally; the inner cases and default handling are otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: This change makes the task state updates for SVE/SME mode selection independent of whether SME is supported by the system. As a result, the function will now always apply the `svcr` streaming-mode bit updates and set the corresponding thread flags for valid vector types, while still rejecting unknown types. It prevents those updates from being skipped when SME support is not reported, which could otherwise leave task state inconsistent.

grouping_result.intent: Always apply SVE/SME task mode state updates regardless of system SME support.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the incorrect dependence on SME support so SVE task mode state updates are applied even on systems with SVE but no SME, preventing the inconsistent TIF_SVE state.

candidates.rationale: This condition incorrectly gates the SVE/SME task-mode update logic on SME support. On systems with SVE but no SME, the body that sets TIF_SVE is skipped, which can leave the task's FP/SVE state inconsistent after an NT_ARM_SVE ptrace write.

This is the state update that should occur for SVE writes, but in the buggy version it was made reachable only when SME is supported. Missing this update on SVE-only systems is the direct inconsistency described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gates the task-mode update logic on SME support. On systems with SVE but no SME, it prevents the code path that sets TIF_SVE from running after an NT_ARM_SVE ptrace write, leading to the inconsistent FP/SVE state described in the root cause.
This is the required state update for SVE writes. In the vulnerable version, it was only reachable under the SME-only condition, so SVE-only systems could save SVE state without setting TIF_SVE.
